own_solution.law: For reflection from a receding panel, the reflected frequency in the air is f_r = 1500(343-6)/(343+6). The recorder recedes from the panel at 9 m/s, so f_received = f_r(343-9)/343. The requested decrease is 1500-f_received.
assumptions: Velocities are measured relative to the still air, except walking velocities along the deck, which are relative to the trolley.
The recorder moves with the trolley unless an added sentence specifies that it is being carried.
The reflected signal reaches the recorder during the stated constant-speed motion.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: TA134 and TA6A4 replace the explicit walking speed of 1.6 m/s in their corresponding numerical renderings with an unspecified 'walking pace', violating the requirement that variants preserve the same number and unit.

notes: The base physics and all individually added sentences give determinate frequency decreases. Initial separation enters propagation times but cancels from the frequency. Carrying the recorder away along the deck makes its air-frame recession speed 10.6 m/s, giving a decrease of 1500[1-(337)(332.4)/(349·343)] = 96.34 Hz. Carrying the toolbox cannot change the recorder velocity when trolley speed is prescribed. Earlier-run statements have no effect on the current measurement. Both distance sentences preserve 82 m. The invalid verdict concerns the stipulated quantitative matching of walking-speed variants, not the solvability of the individual problems.
